en: The Tradition of the Glorious Great Secret (1a) 1. Oṃ, salutations to Mahābhairava.
I bow to the Mother, the venerable Raudrī, who is endowed with the awakening of the command (*ājñā*) that revolves through the fourfold and fivefold subtle [energies],
and who abides as the universe through the sixfold, fivefold, and fourfold revolutions;
she is the progenitor of the great awakening of the bliss of the Command.
A group of four, a group of five, a group of six, a group of four, a group of five, and four;
first, there are the four seats (pīṭhas), and then the four deities of the seats. There is also the pentad of Yoginīs and likewise the hexad of knowledge (jñāna).
One should worship the four Siddhas conjoined with the five jewels; likewise,
one should worship the entire group of nine and sixteen, which is endowed with the eight Kulas and possessed of the six flames.
(1b) One should constantly practice the sequence free from the guru-maṇḍala;
all that [practice] of his becomes fruitless, and he even becomes one who has fallen away from the sequence.
O Mahādeva, one should worship according to the ritual procedure of the *krama*-method.
Upon the *guru-maṇḍala*, one should perform the worship of the *krama-maṇḍala*.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Shkhphreṃ Shūṃ Bhagavati Ambe, for the Vajra-seat, protect, protect the life-force! Hreṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! Thus ends the seat for the protection of the life-force (*jīvarakṣāsana*).

Aiṃ 5. We know Kaulakālī; we meditate upon Mahāmālinī; may that Kubjī inspire us. This is the Gāyatrī. Aiṃ 4. Bhūḥ, salutation. Aiṃ 4. Hrīṃ, Bhuvaḥ, salutation. Aiṃ 4. Śrīṃ, Svaḥ, salutation. Then one should perform the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).
In the root-vidyā, together with the faces, one should perform the binding of the crest-lock (śikhābandha).

*Shkṣmlvryū̃ hrīṃ phaṭ*—one should perform the binding of the crest-lock for the form of Bhairavī. *Aiṃ* salutation to the Dikcarīs; *hrīṃ* salutation to the Bhūcarīs; *śrīṃ* salutation to the Gocarīs; *hreṃ* salutation to the Khecarīs; *shūṃ* salutation to the Vyomacarī.
Aiṃ 4, salutation to those who move through the sky; aiṃ 5, salutation to those who move through the netherworld; aiṃ 4, salutation to those who dwell in the intermediate space.
(2b) Then, one should recollect the Root Vidyā within the interior of the Anāhata lotus: [the goddess] mounted upon a corpse, red in color, and endowed with twelve arms.

One should meditate upon [the deity] who has six faces, eighteen years of age, and bestows all mantras. One should form the tortoise-mudrā (*kūrma-mudrā*). One should recite [the mantra] starting from the place of birth up to the place of the *bindu*.

Then, one should perform the libation for the elements (*bhūta-tarpaṇa*): HŪṂ JUṂ SAḤ | Earth element, satisfy me, satisfy me! SVĀHĀ. HŪṂ JUṂ SAḤ | Water element, satisfy me, satisfy me! SVĀHĀ. HŪṂ JUṂ SAḤ | Fire element, satisfy me, satisfy me! SVĀHĀ.

HŪṂ JUṂ SAḤ, satisfy, satisfy for me the wind element, SVĀHĀ. HŪṂ JUṂ SAḤ, satisfy, satisfy for me the space element, SVĀHĀ. Then the vidyā of the Goddess’s samaya should be recollected. Then one should perform the libation to the ancestors.

HŪṂ JŪṂ SAḤ to the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather; HŪṂ JŪṂ SAḤ to the mother, maternal grandfather, and maternal great-grandfather; HŪṂ JŪṂ SAḤ—may [this] satisfy [them]. May there be abundance of the truth of the goal within the circle of the Guru. Gāyatrī is the essence of all... [namas]. Having thus commenced the rite of worship, placing the right hand below—the mandala situated above, endowed with [the necessary] materials.

(3b) One should cause a triangle, three girdles, and a thick square ground to be made. The auspicious, flawless thread, held in the hand of the jewel-like Guru, should be rotated three times by the Gurus; it should be divided by the former Gurus and established here by the Guru in five ways.

Aiṃ 5 Lāṃ to Śrīkaṇṭha in the east; Aiṃ 5 Vāṃ to Śaṅkara in the south; Aiṃ 5 Śāṃ to Ananta in the west; Aiṃ 5 Ṣaṃ to Sādākhyā in the north; Aiṃ 5 Haṃ to Piṅgala in the center; [Aiṃ to Īśāna] in the northeast; [Aiṃ to Vāyu] in the northwest. Aiṃ Māṃ to Mārjāra in the fire-mandala; Hrīṃ to Ānanda in the southwest corner; Śrīṃ Khecarī in the wind-mandala. One should place the seed-syllable at the tip of the thumb [of the deity] situated in the wind-mandala, together with Śrīnātha Bhairava: Shūṃ. One should worship Laṃ at the station of Ananta, Gaṇeśa, and Vaṭuka, which is the place of the Kṣatradhā: Kṣatradhā Sphreṃ.

(4a) Aiṃ—(glūṃ)—I worship the sandals together with the Mother, the beloved of Gaṇeśanātha. [In the south: Aiṃ 5 (blāṃ blūṃ vaṭu)—I worship the sandals together with the Mother, the beloved of Vaṭukanātha. [In the north: In the west, Aiṃ 5 kṣāṃ kṣīṃ śphreṃ—I worship the sandals of the Mother, the beloved of Sthānakṣetrapāla. Then, with the five *praṇavas*...

One should perform the *karanyāsa* (hand-assignment) three times. With "Aiṃ" on the back of the left hand, "Hrīṃ" on the back of the right hand, "Śrīṃ" on the palm of the left hand, "Shphreṃ" on the palm of the right hand, and "Shūṃ" on the back of the left hand—one purifies the hands three times according to this sequence. Then, one should brandish the weapon (*astra*) with the threefold method for the purpose of protection, employing the six-limbed yoga (*ṣaḍaṅga-yukti*): "Aiṃ 5 Shāṃ, obeisance to the Heart born of nectar;
Shīṃ, Svāhā to the Head garlanded with the splendor of nectar."
Aiṃ 5 śūṃ (Vadhavē) Dhanī Anādisvacchaṃdaśikhāyai vauṣaṭ. Śaiṃ Vajriṇi Vajraghorāya Svataṃtrabodhyakavacāya hūṃ. Aiṃ 5 śauṃ Aluptaśaktinetratrayāya vaṣaṭ.
Aiṃ 5 Śaḥ Ananta-śakti Phreṃ Rakṣa Rakṣa Astrāya Phaṭ. This is the procedure for the placement of the *argha* vessel.

One should prepare the seat with the five *praṇavas*: Aiṃ in the east, Hrīṃ in the south, Śrīṃ in the west, Shphreṃ in the north, and Shūṃ in the center. Having placed the *argha* vessel upon this [seat], one should worship it and fill it completely with wine.

Furthermore, the five *praṇavas* should be deposited again in this sequence; having placed five flowers within the *argha* vessel, one should accomplish the mantra with the *astra* [mantra] and veil it with the *kavaca*.
The wise one should deposit [the seed-syllables] in the center with the root-mantra (*mūla*), worship, and honor them.
May the mantras themselves come, adorned by ten million sacred fords (tīrtha).
One should worship them with water-offerings (argha) and flowers; let the Root-Vidyās [shine] with splendor.
Aiṃ 5 Bhagavati Ambe Hsphreṃ Shphrī̃ Kubjike Shroṃ Shrīṃ Shrauṃ Aghoreśvarī Aghorāmukhe Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi Kiṇi Vicce Hsūṃ 5.
Then one should perform the ritual placement (*karanyāsa*) together with the limbs and faces:
*aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hskhphreṃ (hsvaṃ) bhagavati ambe aṃ aṃ aṃguṣṭhāya śrīādināthapādukābhyo namaḥ | hskhphreṃ shphreṃ kubjike taṃ taṃ tarjanyāyai*.

Salutation to the sandals of Śrī Tejasānandanātha. Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrauṃ Maṃ Maṃ, salutation to the sandals of Śrī Madananātha, the Lord of the Middle Finger. Aghoreśvarī, O Aghorāmukhī! Aṃ Aṃ, salutation to the sandals of Śrī Anāmayanātha, the Lord of the Ring Finger. Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi Kiṇi Vicce Kaṃ Kaṃ, salutation to the sandals of Śrī Kapolanātha, the Lord of the Little Finger. Hskṣmlvryūṃ Shkṣmlvryūṃ, salutation to the sandals of the palms and backs of the hands of Śrī Kaulīśanātha and Śrī Kubjikā Avvā.

(6a) *Hrīṃ vaṃ vaṃ*, at the place of the left wrist: *namaḥ* to the sandals of Māyā. *Daṃ daṃ*, at the place of the right wrist: *namaḥ* to the sandals of Mahāmāyā. *Chāṃ chīṃ kiṇi kiṇi vicce*, *phaṭ* to the clapping of the hands of Anakvanātha. *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ shrūṃ shūṃ*, *namaḥ* to the sandals of Śrī Śivanātha, the supreme goddess (*parādevī*) Śivā, the Mother (*ambe*), for the upward-facing mouth (*ūrdhvavaktra*).

Hsphreṃ shphreṃ Kubjikā! Salutation to the feet of Śrī Vyomanātha, for the eastern face. Shrāṃ shrīṃ shrauṃ! Salutation to the feet of Śrī Vyāpakanātha, for the eastern face, [accompanied] by the mudrā of Siddhayogeśvarī.
Aghoreśvarī! Salutation to the feet of Śrī Jyotirnātha, for the southern face, [addressed] to Kālikā of the non-terrible countenance.

CHĀṂ CHĪṂ KIṆI MAHAṂTĀRIKĀYAI MAHĀLAKṢMYAI UTTARAVAKTRĀYA ŚRĪŚAKTINĀTHAPĀDUKEBHYO NAMAḤ | KIṆI VICCE KUBJIKĀ AVVĀ ĀJÑĀYA PAŚCIMAVAKTRĀYA ŚRĪBINDUNĀTHAPĀDUKEBHYO NAMAḤ || This is the face. AIṂ BHAGAVATI AMBE HR̥TKAMALĀYAI ŚRĪHR̥DAYODAYANĀTHAPĀDUKEBHYO HR̥DAYĀYA NAMAḤ | HSPHREṂ SHPHREṂ KUBJIKEŚIKHAṆḌANĀTHAPĀDUKEBHYO ŚIRASE SVĀHĀ |

*Shrāṃ shrīṃ shrauṃ*, to the crest of Varvaraśikha, to the crest of Śilāśekharanātha, *vauṣaṭ*. *Aghoreśvarī*, to the face of Aghorā and to the sandals of Caṇḍanātha, for the armor, *hūṃ*. *Chāṃ chīṃ kiṇi*, to Mahāntārikā, to Mahālakṣmī, and to the sandals of Śrījyotinātha, for the three eyes, *vaṣaṭ*. *Kiṇi vicce*, to Kubjikā, to the Mother (Avvā), for the Command (*ājñā*), and to the sandals of Śrīanaṅganātha.

*Astrāya phaṭ.* This is the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) [mantra]. *Aiṃ bhagāya namaḥ* at the secret place (*guhya*). *Hrīṃ māyāyai namaḥ* at the navel (*nābhi*). *Śrīṃ lakṣmyāyai namaḥ* at the heart (*hṛdaya*). *Shphreṃ raudrāyai namaḥ* at the mouth (*vaktra*). *Hsūaṃ parātmāya namaḥ* between the eyebrows (*bhrūmadhya*). *Aiṃ* at the left nostril (*vāmanāsāpuṭa*). *Hrīṃ* at the right nostril (*dakṣanāsāpuṭa*). *Śrīṃ* at the left eye (*vāmacakṣus*). *Hsphreṃ* at the right eye (*dakṣacakṣus*). *(Shūṃ)* between the two eyebrows (*bhrūdaṇḍadvayamadhye*). *Aiṃ* on the forehead (*lalāṭa*). *Hrīṃ* at the right ear (*dakṣakarṇa*). *Śrīṃ* at the left ear (*vāmakarṇa*).
*Hsphreṃ* at the nape of the neck (*kṛkoṭikā*). *Hsūaṃ* above the head (*mastaka*). This is the *mūrtikośanyāsa* (the ritual placement of the sheath of forms).

(7b) Then one should perform the consecration of the ritual substances (*dravya-saṃskāra*): *Shaṃ saṃjīvani saṃjīvani* for the flowers; *hrīṃ paramanādinī* for the incense (*dhūpa*); *śrīṃ paramāmṛtāyai* for the sandalwood; *hrīṃ anantabalaparākramāyai* for the water offering (*argha*);
*hsphreṃ jyotirūpātmane* for the light of the lamps (*jyotiḥ*).

One should sprinkle these substances for consecration with the *argha* vessel. Then, one should worship or cause to be worshipped the five jewels (*pañcaratna*) within the *argha* vessel together with the [five] objects of sense. *Glūṃ*, I worship the sandals of Nandanātha, the ear-element Brahma-jewel and the object of sound. *Slūṃ*, I worship the sandals of Nandanātha, the skin-element Viṣṇu-jewel and the object of touch.

Plūṃ: I worship the sandals of Ānandanātha, who has become the ancient eye and the object of sight. Mlūṃ: I worship the sandals of Ānandanātha, who has become the lordly jewel-tongue and the object of taste.
Nlūṃ: I worship the sandals of Ānandanātha, who has become the Sadāśiva-jewel-nose and the object of smell. Then, one should touch one’s own body with the arghya vessel:
"Born from a fragment of the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), arising from the entirety of essences..."
One should bring the nectar (*peyūṣa*) as the *argha* offering, filling the great vessel.
*Sahakṣamalavarayū̃ hasakṣamalavarayū̃ śrīānandabhairavāya vauṣaṭ*. Surādevī, flow, flow with nectar, *svāhā*.
After having established the *nīti* within the vessel, one should subsequently visualize [the deity];
[one should meditate on] that which resembles the abundant sun and possesses a splendor equal to ten million moons.
In its center, one should contemplate the triangular fire-maṇḍala containing a *bindu*.

One should contemplate that vessel being filled with that supreme nectar, which possesses the immense brilliance of lightning and flows forth. In its center, one should visualize the Goddess, whose radiance is equal to that of a ruby.
Then, one should invoke the entire maṇḍala of the gurus:
*aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śphreṃ śūṃ*, "We know Śrīkaṇṭha; may we meditate upon the Great Siddha; may Kaulī inspire us. *Aiṃ* to the feet of the Brahmā-throne. *Aiṃ*. (9a) *{5}*

Having offered the sixfold seat— *aiṃ 5* for the Viṣṇu-seat, *aiṃ 5* for the Rudra-seat, *aiṃ 5* for the Īśvara-seat, *aiṃ 5* for the Sadāśiva-seat, and *aiṃ 5* for the Lion-seat (*siṃhāsana*)— and having uttered *hskhphreṃ śkhphreṃ*, one should cause [the Goddess] to be seated there.
O God, without a seat, the deity cannot be worthy of worship.

Ā Ū Āgaccha āgaccha! O Śrī Kubjikādevī, together with your retinue, I invoke you—she who is the supreme and lower power (Parāparā-śakti), who resides in the sky, whose nature is the void, who dwells within the lotus of the moon and sun; come to my maṇḍala!
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hskhphreṃ Shūṃ! O Blessed Mother, Hskhphreṃ Shkhphreṃ Kubjike Shrāṃ Śrīṃ Shrauṃ Aghoreśvarī, O you whose face is non-terrible (Aghorāmukhe)!
(9b) Having first worshipped *chāṃ chīṃ kiṇi kiṇi vicce shū̃ shkhphrẽ śrī̃ hrī̃ aiṃ* in the center, one should then worship the triad of Śāmbhavīs on the girdle (*mekhalā*). [The mantra is:
*shrū̃ śrīvastunāthādhikāre hrī̃ kulakaulīsiddhājñā hskhphrẽ manonmanī kubjikājñā valī avvā shkṣmlvryūṃ*.

I worship the sandals of Śrī Sandhyānanda Deva, Śrī Tṛṣṇīśanātha, and Śrī Nātha. Śrūṃ! In the authority of Śrī Merunātha: Khphreṃ! Mahākālī, the Command of the Kula, Manonmanī, Vakradevī, Ājñāvalī, and Avvā; sahakṣamalavarayūṃ! I worship the sandals of Śrī Śrīnātha, Kaulīśa Bhairava, and Śrī Kubjikā, together with Avvā.

(10a) Śrūṃ! In the section on the Principle of the Self (*ātmatattva*), I worship the sandals of the venerable Śrīnātha, Uḍīśanātha, and Śrīśrīnātha—[empowered by] the command of Kāla and Kālī, *khphrè*, the Transmental (*unmanī*) command of Kubjikā, the powerful *avvā* [seed-syllable], and *śkṣmlvryū̃*. This is the triad of Sāmbhava.

Khphreṃ! In the glorious garden of Mahācaṇḍagogeśvarī, at the Mahāmudrā-pīṭha, I worship with my sandals Oḍīśanātha, Oḍā Avvā, Ādhārīśadeva (Raktā) Devī, Śaṅkhamaṭhaka, the Kadamba tree, Veṇī, Indravāruṇī, Khecarīmudrā, the Kadaṃba cave, Karavīra, the Siṃha cremation ground, Vaṭuka, Agnimukha Kṣetrapāla, Kṛtayuga, Khageṃdranātha, and Vijjā Avvā, together with their sandals.
Aiṃ 5 Khā RṢRĪṂ! To Śrījālāṃdhara, the great maṇḍala-pīṭha; to Jālīśanātha; to Jālā Avvā; to Ādhāracakrīśa; to the goddess Mahākālī;

to Jyotirmaṭha; to Bilvavṛkṣavilī; to Devadāyā; to Kuraṅgiṇī; to the Nirvāṇa-guhā mudrā; to Laṅguḍa; to the cremation ground; to Kapila; to Vaṭuka; to Jayantī; to Kṣetrapāla; to Kūrmanātha of the Tretā Yuga; to Maṅgalāvā—[I worship] together with the sandals.

O Śrī Pūrṇagiri, Great Seat of Mantras; O Pūrṇīśanātha; O Pūrṇā Avvā; O Kuraṅgīśadeva; O Cāmuṇḍādevī; O Yakṣiṇī; O Maṭhaciñciṇī; O Vṛkṣavallī marked with the wheel! I worship [you]. In the south. In the Dvāpara Yuga, I worship the Lelihāna-mudrā, Śivaguhā, Dīpa, Śmaśāna, Piṅgala, Vaṭuka, Pātava, Karṇa, Kṣetrapāla, Meṣanātha, Kāmamaṅgalā, and Avvā, together with the Pādukā, on the left.
Aiṃ 5 Phreṃ Caṇḍikāpālinī Svāhā. Ghaṃ!

I worship the venerable Kāmāśanātha of the great seat (Mahāpīṭha) of Śrī-Kāmarūpa, Kāmā, Avvā, Madeṃdreśa, Deva, Mahaukṣmādevī, Anāmayamaṭhaka, Ṭāha, Vṛkṣavellī, Aparājitā, Jagadyonimudrā, and Manodbhavā.
In Guhā, [I worship] Bhayāpahā, Śmaśāna, Kṛśodarī, Vaṭuka, Gajakumbha, Kṣetrapāla, Kaliyuga, Maccheṃdranātha, Kuṅkaṇā, and Avvā, together with the sandals (pādukā). In front:

(11b) one should then worship this group of four seats (pīṭha) and the seat of the lineage of gurus (gurupaṃkti-āsana). Aiṃ 5 Hskhphreṃ, I worship the sandals for the Ātmatattva; Śrāṃ, for the Vidyātattva; Hsphreṃ, for the Śivatattva. I worship the sandals.

Aiṃ 5. I worship the venerable mother Śrī Candragarbhādanātha together with her sandals. Aiṃ 5. I worship the venerable mother Muktānandadevamahānātha together with her sandals. Aiṃ 5. I worship the venerable mother Śrī Sahajakhecaralalitānandadevacandrā, the Gaṅgā mother, together with her sandals. Aiṃ 5. I worship the venerable mother Somānandadevānandadevī together with her sandals. (12a)

Aiṃ 5. I worship the *pādukā* of Śrī Līlānandadeva together with Queen Udayādevī and the Mother (Avvā). Aiṃ 5. I worship the *pādukā* of Śrī Nāgānandadeva together with Queen Salādevī and the Mother (Avvā).

Aiṃ 5. I worship the *pādukā* of Śrī Śaktyānandadeva together with Ātmaśakti and Icchāśakti. Thus, one should worship the six [deities] including oneself. One should worship them before the Krama on top of one's own head.

Then, the Root-Vidyā consisting of thirty-two syllables is to be worshipped in the center; thereafter, the five jewels are to be worshipped in sequence: Aiṃ 5 U Brahmadeva Hskhphreṃ! To Manonmanā, Glūṃ Gaganāmṛtaratnagarbhabhogavāsinī, the sixty-four thousand million Yoginīs, Vijjā, Avvā, Pādagūḍhaguhyagambhīraviśvakṣārapārthivādāravṛhadbrahman— I worship your sandals.

Aiṃ 5 (Caṃ) (Viṣṇu) Deva Hskhphreṃ! To Vyāpinyā, the Mistress of thirty-two thousand, lakṣas, and koṭis of Yoginīs, who dwells in the enjoyment of the jewel-womb of celestial nectar; who is skillful, the Mother (Avvā), whose feet are cooled by the water of the auspicious Śiva, and who possesses the pervasive glory of the Apavarga and Varuṇa realms—I worship the sandals of Viṣṇudeva.

Aiṃ 5 Chaṃ Śrī Rudradeva HSKHPHREṂ Sama- - PLŪṂ! I worship the sandal-dust from the feet of the venerable Mother Śrī Vidyutmālā Avvā—the mistress of sixteen thousand, hundred thousand, and ten million Yoginīs, and the goddess Ratnagarbhabhogavāsinī of the nectar of the wind—who brilliantly inflames with her radiant flames the sandals of Śrī Rudradeva. Aiṃ 5 Jaṃ Śrī Īśvaradeva (HSKHPHREṂ) Avyaktāya SLŪṂ! [I worship] the goddess Ratnagarbhabhogavāsinī of the nectar of mortals, [and her retinue of] eight hundred thousand and ten million Yoginīs.
I worship the sandals of the Lord in the form of the vital breath (*prāṇa*), which is the wind arising from the fire of the lotus-feet of the Mother (*Avvā*) born of one’s own [body].

*Oṃ* 5 *jhaṃ* Sadāśiva-deva *hskhphreṃ*, to Nādinyāya, *nlūṃ*, to the Nāgāmṛta-ratnagarbha-bhogavāsinī, the Mistress of four hundred thousand million Yoginīs, *khiṃkhinī*, I worship the sandals of the Mother (*Avvā*) at the end of Sadāśiva in the upper wheel (*ūrddhvacakra*), which is the unobscured space of the Mother’s feet.
(13b) Thus one should worship the Five Jewels: *hsphrāṃ saṃjīvani saṃjīvani sarvajñatā-hṛdayāya namaḥ*. *hsphrīṃ ūrddhakeśe parāpare śirase svāhā*.
*hsphrūṃ prajvalitaśikhe nādinī śikhāyai vauṣaṭ*. *hsphre vidyujjihve aghoreśvarī-kavacāya hūṃ*. *hsphrauṃ tārakākṣe mahādīpte*.

Vaṣaṭ to the three eyes, most brilliantly blazing! Hsphraḥ! Māraṇi māraṇi, O Śivā, command! Phaṭ to the weapon! Hsaphraṃ! Saṃjīvani saṃjīvani, [bestow] omniscience! Namaḥ to the upward-facing mouth! Hsphrīṃ! Namaḥ to the eastern face with hair standing erect! Hsphrūṃ! [O you] who roar with a crest of blazing flames!

Homage to the southern face: *hsphreṃ* Vidyujjihva Aghoreśvara. Homage to the northern face: *hsphrauṃ* Tārākṣa Mahādīptatara. Homage to the western face: *hsphraṃ* Māraṇī Ājñāśiva Parāparavaktra. One should thus perform the worship of these limbs and faces. (Five *aiṃ*s)—the Root Vidya is to be worshipped in the center. *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hshrīṃ hshrūṃ Bhagavati Ambe hskhphreṃ shkhphreṃ Kubjike (hsrāṃ hsrīṃ hsrauṃ) Aghoreśvari Aghorāmukhe chāṃ chīṃ kiṇi kiṇi.*

(14b) *Vicce hsvrūṃ hskhphrī̃ śrī̃ hrīṃ aiṃ*. One should worship this goddess of the samaya, consisting of thirty-two syllables and enclosed by the five *praṇavas*, in the center. Then, one should bind the three mudrās: first the lotus mudrā (*padmamudrā*), then the womb mudrā (*yonimudrā*). Thereafter, one should worship within the *navātmā* maṇḍala. One should place [the mantra] five times in the north: "I worship the sandals of Sabhānandanātha-Brahmāṇī together with Avvā."

Aiṃ 5 (Svayaṃ) Īśānamaṇḍala. I worship the pādukā together with the Mother (Avvā), Halakulīśānandanātha and Māheśvarī. Aiṃ 5, one should place [the mantra] in the southwest: I worship the pādukā together with the Mother (Avvā), Kūṭāṅkṣasaṃvartānandanātha and Vaiṣṇavī. Aiṃ 5, Viṃ—kraṃ, in the south: I worship the pādukā together with the Mother (Avvā), Mahākālānandanātha and Vārāhī.

Aiṃ 5! In the east, I worship the sandals together with the deity Puraṃdara, the mother Indrāṇī, and Ānandanātha. Aiṃ 5! In the west, [I worship] Varuṇa—[the deity] Khaḍgīśāna, the mother Cāmuṇḍā, and Ānandanātha—together with the sandals. Aiṃ 5! In the southeast (vahnikoṇe), [I worship] Agni—the serpent-deity Abhujaṅga, the mother Kaumārī, and Ānandanātha—together with the sandals. Aiṃ 5! In the northwest (vāyukoṇe), one should place Cala.

I worship the sandals together with the Mother Mahālakṣmī, the mistress of the Pravālya grove. Aiṃ Bhagavati Ambe Hsphreṃ Shphreṃ Kubjike Hsrāṃ Hsrīṃ Hsrauṃ Aghoreśvarī Aghorāmukhe Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi Kiṇi Vicce Hsphrūṃ 5 Ūṃ. I worship the sandals together with the Mother Kubjikā, the mistress of Nauka.

In the center: *ṢKṢMLVRYŪṂ*. Then, one should form the *yonimudrā*. Thereafter, one should worship the command (*ājñā*) that has arisen from the sixteen *Nāthas*: *HSKHPHREṂ*. I worship the sandals together with the venerable mother Śrīcandrapuranātha-Śrīcandraprabhā. In the west: *HSKHPHREṂ ŚRĪṂ*. I worship the sandals together with the venerable mother Gulmanātha-Śrīgahanaprabhā. In the north: *HSKHPHREṂ* (16a).

In the east: I worship the sandals together with Śrī Stambhanātha and Śrī Sthūlaprabhā Avvā. Hasakhaphrē: I worship the sandals together with Śrī Karpāśānandanātha and Śrī Kamalāprabhā Avvā. Hskhphrē: I worship the sandals together with Śrī Vaṭapuranātha and Vaṭaprabhā Avvā. In the northeast: Hskhphrē: I worship the sandals together with Śrī Vīranātha and Śrī Vīraprabhā Avvā. In the southwest: Hsphrē: I worship the sandals together with Śrī Prayāsanātha and Śrī Pañcaprabhā Avvā.

To Agni: *hsphreṃ*, I worship the *pādukā* together with Śrīkaṃśālānandanātha, Śrīkaṃlālaprabhā, and Avvā. (16b) To Vāyavya: *hsphrẽ*, I worship the *pādukā* together with Śrībhogapurānandanātha, Śrībhogaprabhā, and Avvā. To the northwest of Vāyu: *hsphrẽ*, [I worship] Śrībimbadevanātha.

I worship the sandals together with the venerable Śrībimbaprabhā. Hsphreṃ! I worship the sandals together with the venerable Śrīkhaḍgadevanātha and the venerable Śrīkhaḍgaprabhā. (Hsphreṃ! I worship the sandals together with the venerable Śrīrudradevanātha and the venerable Śrīrudraprabhā. (Hsphreṃ! I worship the sandals together with the venerable Śrīdhariṇīdevanātha and the venerable Śrīdevaprabhā. Hsphreṃ! I worship the sandals together with the venerable Śrīmudra-ṭanātha and the venerable Śrīmadhuraprabhā.
Hsphrẽ Śrīvaṅkāpuradevaśrīvaraprabhā Avvā—I worship the sandals. Hsphrẽ Śrībhojadevanāthaśrībhojaprabhā Avvā together with [the others]—I worship the sandals.

By this sequence mentioned previously, one should then worship the Samayā Devī in the center. One should worship her by means of the thirty-two syllables joined with the five *praṇavas*. Then, beginning from the east, one should worship Hetukā and the others.

One should worship as far as the northeast (Aiśāna). In the east: *Hskhphreṃ* to the Śrī Hetuka, together with *Hrīṃ* Śrī Herambā and Avvā, I worship the *pādukā*. In the southeast (Āgneya): *Hasakhphreṃ* to the Śrī Agnivetāla, together with *Hrīṃ* Agniśikhā and Avvā, I worship the *pādukā*. In the south (Yāmya): ... [text continues] ... 17b) ... I worship the *pādukā* together with Avvā.

Hskhphreṃ! To Agnijihva, together with his consort Hrīṃ Anantaprabhā, I worship the sandals. [In the] Southwest. Hskhphreṃ! To Śrī Kālākhyā, together with his consort Hrīṃ Kālasaṃkarṣaṇī, I worship the sandals. [In the] West. Hskhphreṃ! To Śrī Kāpālin, together with his consort Hrīṃ Śrī Kumudā, I worship the sandals. [In the] Northwest. Hskhphreṃ! To Śrī Ekapāda, together with his consort Hrīṃ Śrī Ekalavīrā...
I worship [him] together with the sandals. Kubera.

(18a) Ha Sa Kha Phreṃ! To the illustrious Bhīmarūpa, Hrīṃ! To the illustrious Bhīmabhadra and the Mother (Avvā), I worship [them] together with the sandals. — — — — — — — — one should worship the maṇḍala of the Guru together with his retinue.

Then one should worship the Samaya-vidyā. One should worship with substances such as *ravati* for the purpose of completing the central maṇḍala. This is the complete Guru-maṇḍala. Aiṃ—[one should worship] the Supreme Goddess, the Mistress of the Host, who is seated upon a lotus throne [consisting of] Sana, Rudra, and Vajra, and who has entered the sixfold [path].
Salutations to that [Śrī Guru] by whom [the world] was dried up at the time of the dissolution,
and by whom it was brought back to life; salutations to the Guru who is like a lamp of the moon, by whom the moon was beheld.
— — — — — — salutation to that venerable guru (namaḥ) | (18b)
— — — — the reality heard [by me], whose sphere transcends the path of speech.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state has been revealed.
I bow to that Maṇḍala, which extends as far as the seven oceans, endowed with the seven continents, and possessing the form of an unbroken circle.

Then, upon the surface of the Guru-maṇḍala, one should worship the Krama-maṇḍala. With saffron mixed with *vidyā*, as well as red pigment (*raktavadana*) combined with *alika* and camphor—or alternatively, mixed with the ashes of a hero (*vīrabhasman*)—one should prepare it in the center. Outside of that, one should fashion a vajra-lotus girdle (*mekhalā*). Outside of that, one should fashion a square marked with four doors.

Furthermore, one should perform [the ritual] again by means of the application of the limbs (*aṅga*) and faces (*vaktra*) as previously established. Again, one should perform the placement of the *argha* vessel according to this sequence. One should touch one’s own body with the *argha* vessel. [Mahāmālinī-vidyā]: "We know Mahāmālinī; we meditate on the Agitator of the Mind; may Kubjī impel us. Then, one should perform the sixfold placement (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*). Alternatively, one should perform the placement of Śabdarāśimālinī: *Aiṃ 5 Aṃ*—to Śrīkaṇṭha at the head; *Ā*—to Ananteśa at the face.

*I* for Sūkṣma on the right eye; *I* for Trimūrti on the left eye; *U* for Amarīśa on the right ear; *Ū* for Aghīśa on the left ear; *Ṛ* for Bhārabhūti on the right nostril; *Ṝ* for Atīśa on the left nostril; *LṚ* for Sthāṇu on the right cheek; *LṜ* for Hara on the left cheek; *E* for Jhaṇṭīśa on the lower row of teeth.

Ai to Bhautika on the upper row of teeth; O to Sadyojāta on the lower lip; Au to Anugrahīśa on the upper lip; Aṃ to Krūra at the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra); Aḥ to Mahāsena at the root of the tongue. Aiṃ 5 Śrī Kaulīśanātha Kubjikā Avvā, protect, protect the head! Aiṃ 5 Ka to Krodhīśa on the right shoulder; Kha to Caṇḍīśa on the right elbow; Ga to Pañcārtha on the forearm of the right arm.

(20a) *Gha* for Śiva on the bracelet of the right hand; *ṅa* for Ekarudra on the nails of the fingers of the right hand; *aiṃ 5* for Brahmāṇī—may she protect—the forearm of the right arm; *aiṃ 5 ca* for Kūrma on the left shoulder; *cha* for Ekanetra on the left elbow; *aiṃ 5 ja* for Caturānana on the forearm of the left arm; *aiṃ 5 jha* for Ajitānanā on the bracelet of the left hand; *aiṃ 5 ña* for Śarman on the nails of the fingers of the left hand.

AṂ 5: Thus, one should protect Māheśvarī on the left upper arm. AṂ ṬA: To Someśvara, on the right buttock. AṂ ṬHA: To Lāṅgalīśa, on the right thigh. AṂ ḌA: To Dāruka, on the right calf. AṂ ḌHA: To Arddhanārīśvara, on the right foot. AṂ ṆA: To Umākānta, on the nails of the toes of the right foot. (20b)

Aiṃ 5 Śrīkaumārī protect the right calf. Aiṃ 5 Taṃ Āṣāḍhīśa on the left buttock. Tha Diṇḍīśa on the left thigh. Da Dhātrīśa on the left calf. Dha Mīneśa on the left foot. Na Meśa on the nails of the toes of the left foot. Aiṃ 5 Śrīvaiṣṇavī protect the left calf. Aiṃ 5 Pa Lohitā on the right side of the belly.
Pha Śikhīśa on the left side of the belly. Ba Chagalaṇḍa on the back. Bha Dviraṇḍa on the abdomen. Ma Mahākāla on the hips. Ya Vālīśa on the skin.

(21a) AṂ HŪṂ: May Indrāṇī protect [me] always in the blood, for Bhujaṅgeśa; RAKṢA: for Ulapinākīśa; MĀṂSA: for Khaḍgīśa; SNĀYU: AIṂ HŪṂ: may Indrāṇī protect [me] always in those [tissues]. AIṂ HŪṂ ŚA: for Vāgīśvara, in the bones; ṢA: for Śvetarudra, in the marrow; SA: for Bhṛgvānanda, in the semen; HALA: for Kulīśa, in the vital breath. AIṂ HŪṂ: May Śrī Cāmuṇḍā protect [me] in all the joints of the limbs. AIṂ HŪṂ KṢA: for Saṃvarta, in the wrath.

Aiṃ 5 Śrī Mahālakṣmī, protect me in all the limbs and sub-limbs! Aiṃ 5 Maṃ, salutation to the heart. Aiṃ 5 Aṃ, svāhā to the head. Aḥ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock. Ya, hūṃ to the armor. Aiṃ 5 I I, vaṣaṭ to the eyes. Aiṃ Kṣaḥ, phaṭ to the weapon. Thus ends the Śabdarāśi Nyāsa.

(21b) *Aiṃ* is *Nādinī* on the crest-lock; *tha* is *Grasanī* for the head; *ṛ* is *Nivṛtti*, *ṝ* is *Pratiṣṭhā*, *lṛ* is *Vidyā*, and *lṝ* is *Śānti*—these four are on the garland of the heads. *Ca* is *Cāmuṇḍā* on the upper eye; *dha* is *Priyadarśanī* on the two eyes; *ṇa* is *Nārāyaṇī* on the ears; *u* is *Mohanī* as the ornament of the right ear; *ū* is for *Prajñā* as the ornament of the left ear.

I is for Guhyaśakti on the nose; Va is for Vajriṇī on the mouth; Ka is for Karālī; Kha is for Kapālī; Ga is for Śivā; Gha is for Ghorā; Ṅa is for Thirvvarā. [These are] the two rows of teeth, upper and lower. A is for Vāgīśvarī on the speech; I is for Sarasvatī on the tongue; Va is for Śikhivāhinī on the throat. (22a)

*Bha* is Bhīṣaṇī on the tip of the right arm; *ya* is Vāyuvegā on the tip of the left arm; *ḍa* is Lāmā on the right arm; *ṭa* is Vināyakī on the left arm; *ṭha* is Pūrṇimā on both hands; *jha* is Jhaṅkāriṇī on the nails of the fingers of the right hand; *ñaṃ* is Kūrdhanīśā on the nails of the fingers of the left hand; *ra* is Dīpanī on the right hand; [the syllable for] the Trident-staff (*triśūladaṇḍa*) is on the backbone; *ja* is Jayantī on the trident above the right staff; *ṭa* is Kapālinī on the skull-cup in the left hand; *pa* is Pāvanī at the heart.

*Sa* is for Paramātmā in the *jīva*; *ha* is for Ambikā in the vital breath (*prāṇa*); *aḥ* is for Icchāśakti and Buddhi; *cha* is for Chagalaṇḍī in the right breast; *la* is for Pūtanā in the left breast; *ā* is for Āmoṭī in the milk; *ṣa* is for Lambodarī in the belly; *kṣaḥ* is for Saṃhāriṇī in the nose; *ma* is for Mahākālī on the hips; *aṃ* is for Kusumāyudhā in the private parts; *śa* is for Śukrādevī in the semen; *ta* is for Tārā on the two thighs.

E, the power of knowledge (*jñānaśakti*), on the right knee. Ai, the power of compassion (*kṛpāśakti*), on the left knee. O, Gāyatrī, on the right calf. Au, Sāvitrī, on the left calf. Da, Dahanī, on the right foot. Pha, Phetkārī, on the left foot. Aiṃ Rhrāṃ, salutation to the upward face. Rhrīṃ, salutation to the eastern face. Rhrūṃ, salutation to the southern face. (23a)

*rhraiṃ* salutation to the northern face; *rhrauṃ* salutation to the western face; *rhraḥ* salutation to the supreme-and-non-supreme face. *rhrāṃ* salutation to the heart; *rhrī̃* svāhā to the head; *rhrū̃* vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock; *rhraĩ* hūṃ to the armor; *rhraũ* vaṣaṭ to the three eyes; *rhraḥ* phaṭ to the weapon. Thus is the Mālinī-nyāsa. Again, one should worship Gaṇeśa, Vaṭuka, and Kṣetrapāla, as well as the offering for the Yoginīs.

One should cause [the ritual] to be performed. One should worship the *arghapātra* vessel. One should perform the *dūtīnyāsa*. Aiṃ 5 Kālikāli Mahākāli, O consumer of flesh and blood, protect! O black-faced goddess, let not the enemy see me! *Namaḥ* to the heart. Aiṃ! Homage to the Blessed One, Ucchiṣṭacaṇḍālinī, consumer of human blood and flesh, bearer of the skull-bowl and the *khaṭvāṅga* staff! Slay, slay! (23b)
Daha daha, dhama dhama, paca paca, śīghra śīghra, āveśaya āveśaya, hara hara, Śaṅkari, devour [the name], devour! To the head, Svāhā!

Aiṃ Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrauṃ, O you of blazing crests, O Aghorī, O you with a terrifying face, O Garlanded-with-Flames, O bearer of the form of the self-willed crest, O beginningless self-willed crest, Vauṣaṭ to the crest! Aiṃ (five times), O you who lift up, O you who strike down, O you who completely crush all enemies, O you who pierce, O you who tear asunder, O you who strike down all wicked ones, Hūṃ to the armor! Aiṃ, protect, protect! Descend!

(24a) Descend, O Mistress of Cāmuṇḍā! Hūṃ! Vaṣaṭ to the three eyes! Aiṃ! O Guhyakubjikā, hūṃ phaṭ! Strike down, strike down all my misfortunes—those [caused by] yantras, mantras, tantras, and practiced applications, whether performed by someone, caused to be performed, or which they will perform in the future! O you who are terrifying with tusks! Hrīṃ phreṃ hrūṃ hūṃ! Phaṭ to the weapon!
Having worshipped the heart in the southeast, the head in the domain of Īśāna (the northeast),
one should place the crest-lock in the northwest corner and the armor in the southwest.
The eye is to be known as being in the center, and the weapon in the cardinal and intermediate directions.

Therefore, one should perform the invocation as before. In the *krama-maṇḍala*, one should worship the six seats of the Goddess: "Aiṃ, I worship the sandal of the seat of Brahmā. (24b) "Aiṃ 5, [I worship] the sandal of the seat of Śrī Viṣṇu; Aiṃ 5, [I worship] the sandal of the seat of Śrī Rudra; Aiṃ 5, [I worship] the sandal of the seat of Śrī Īśvara; Aiṃ 5, [I worship] the sandal of the seat of Śrī Sadāśiva."
Aiṃ 5, the sandals of Śrī Bhairavāsana. Thus, one should offer [the worship] in the same sequence as before. Then, one should worship the five pillars (khaṃbha):
Aiṃ 5, I worship the sandals of Śikheśvara-khaṃbha. In the east. Aiṃ 5, Saṃ, I worship the sandals of Vīreśvara-khaṃbha. In the south.
Aiṃ 5. I worship the sandals of Śrīkuleśvarastambha in the west. Aiṃ 5. I worship the sandals of Saṃkulastambha in the north. Aiṃ 5. I worship the sandals of Haṃ Anaccastambha in the center.

(25a) Therefore, one should worship Śrīkaṇṭha and the others. According to this sequence: Śrīkaṇṭha, Śaṃkara, Ananta, Sādākhya, and likewise Piṅgala—these five are the creators of emanation and the ones who bring down the Kulakaula.

Śrīkaṇṭha is to be known as earth, and Śaṃkara is said to be water. Ananta is called fire, and Sādākhya is said to be wind. And Piṅgala is indeed space, according to the sequence of the emergence from the Brahman-tattva.
That power which is both immanent and transcendent is the causal attribute;
when that descends upon men, they then become vessels for liberation.
Oṃ Bhagavati Ambe!

(25b) *Hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryūṃ kubjike hsrāṃ hsrīṃ hsrauṃ aghoreśvari aghorāmukhe chāṃ chīṃ kiṇi kiṇi vicce śrvūṃ*—these five [syllables] are to be worshipped in the center. Then, the triad of *Sāṃbhava* is to be worshipped on the girdle (*mekhalā*). *Hsvūṃ*: within the authority of the venerable Śambhunātha is the venerable Kulakaulinī, the Siddha-command (*siddhājñā*), *Hskhphreṃ*, Manonmanī, the command of Kubjikā.

Dance, dance! Gape, gape! (O you who possess the form of the three worlds, O Śrī-Śrī! Drive away, drive away those who revolve a thousand times! Truṭa, truṭa! Ciri, ciri! Hiri, hiri! Bhiri, bhiri! Terrify, terrify! Cause to wander, cause to wander! Cause to flee!
*Drāvaṇi kṣobhaṇi kṣobhaṇi māraṇi māraṇi saṃjīvani saṃjīvani heri heri giri giri śu-śu-* (40a) ... (layādi).
*Aiṃ namo mātṛgaṇāya hrāṃ namo namaḥ | Vicce svāhā*. With this salutation, the initiate (*samayin*) should fulfill the commitment (*samaya*).

Having offered three handfuls of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity. One should meditate with focused visualization (*bhāvanā*). [The mantra] ending in *lyādi*—one should cause the mind to enter the power (*śakti*).
Having brought day and night to an end, through the worship of the sequence (*kramārcana*)—one should utter the sequence-knowledge (*kramavidyā*): *aiṃ hrīṃ*—*ni*—[etc.]—*iha avalokite*.
(rhrā̃ rhrī̃ rhraũ) (garbhāmā)linī kili kili kaḥ khphrẽ lala apaṭhanīya (41a)
Her form was adorned with infinite beauty, difficult even for the gods to attain;
her feet were decorated with endless anklets.
On the region of his waist, Takṣaka shone as a girdle;
Kārkoṭaka was placed as a bracelet, and Vāsuki was situated upon his neck.
Having made Kulika his crown, Gonāsā served as his earrings.
Furthermore, those who belong to other naga lineages [are present] on the armlet and ring.
A lotus is situated on the right staff, while Mahāpadma is on the left;
[he holds] a khaṭvāṅga, a noose, the gesture of fearlessness, a rosary, and a book.
In her [left] hand she holds a small knife (*kaṭṭāraka*), and likewise a conch-shell (*saṃkhapāla*) above it;

in her right hands, the goddess holds a skull-bowl (*kapāla*), the gesture of granting boons (*varada*), a sword (*khaḍga*), a trident (*triśūla*), a goad (*aṅkuśa*), and a mirror (*darpaṇa*)— these are the five substances (*dravyapañcaka*) in the right hands of the goddess.
Filled with great splendor and joined with the wish-fulfilling gem of stainless thought,
one should constantly meditate with devotion upon this supreme sixfold posture.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—
[all gaze upon] the state of a ghost (pretatva), most terrible and fearsome, seated upon the throne. O Mahādevī, I meditate upon you who possess such [power] and are in the bloom of youth.
This goddess, mounted upon the wheel-like [tradition] of the Kula teaching,
shall manifest in the Kali age as the supreme Western Tradition (Paścimāmnāya).
Having always recognized her form in this way, he who is liberated shall liberate many others.
Then one should ask for forgiveness and recite the three sūtras:
"Mālinī, the Pīṭhas, and Mahāmāyā.
Then one should ask for forgiveness and perform the entire ritual service (*carucāra*).
One should cause [the disciple] to consume [the substance] mixed with honey and molasses in the proper sequence before him,
so that through a state free from secret signs no sense of duality arises.
They move among one another in accordance with the order of seniority.
Then, one should ask for forgiveness, perform the worship, and commence the dismissal (*visarjana*).
[One should visualize the deity] seated upon the throne of the syllable *Aiṃ*, stationed atop a vajra-lotus.
I bow to the Goddess known as Śrī Kubjikā, who has entered the sixfold path;
I bow to the Mother known as Śrī Kubjikā, who is established upon the seat of the Yoginīs, who proclaims the Śrīkrama, and who bestows eternal bliss.
I bow to the one named Śrī Kubjikā, whose nature is the manifold form, who arises from the realization of the Command, and who possesses the sixfold movement of the spies.
Arising from the *kaṇḍa*, she is of the nature of fire; having reached the heart, she is of the nature of the sun;
arising from the palate, she is of the nature of the moon. Thus established in one place in three ways, the Goddess is the channel of the triple abode, filling the three *trikas*.
Whatever Yoginīs there may be—whether fierce, gentle, or terrible;
whether moving in the sky, moving on the earth, or the Sustainer—may they always be pleased with me.
Whatever I perform by deed, mind, or speech, [may it be auspicious].

Since she was impelled by that power, therefore forgive me everything. Salutations to that illustrious Guru, by whom the *ciñciṇī* tree was withered in the terrible forest in the place of the Mother, and by whom it was restored to life once again.
In the terrible Mahālakṣmī forest, his foot was split by a *bilva* tree;
I bow to that foot, which is renowned as the wheel of the three worlds. (43a)

Salutations to that illustrious Guru by whom that Truth— ineffable, unheard, and beyond the range of the path of speech— has been revealed as that supreme state. [Salutations] to him who [grants] the earth bounded by the seven oceans and endowed with the seven continents.
I bow to that auspicious one whose form is an unbroken circle.
Hrīṃ rhsphrīṃ hrīṃ phreṃ ryrūṃ!
Go, go to the supreme abode where the Stainless One dwells.
May all the deities go to their own abodes and take refuge in their respective places. Hrīṃ rhrīṃ rhrīṃ phaṭ svāhā!
May the lineages of practitioners rejoice, having attained the supernatural powers such as *aṇimā* and the rest.
May that indescribable Sāṃbhavī, who is the primordial Siddhā and who resides equally within the yoginīs of all sense-objects, remove [all obstacles]. (44a)
In which [tradition] the Guru’s lotus-feet alone have been obtained.

Thus ends the Śrīkrama in the Mahārahasya Saṃpradāya. May there be prosperity! Victory to the King of Kings, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Sovereign, the illustrious Arimalla Deva! Year 331, the seventh day of the bright fortnight of Śrāvaṇa.
